one_liner: Discord offers a free, self-serve REST/Gateway API with OAuth2 and bot tokens; only community MCP servers are likely (none verified in the pages).
auth_notes: Three documented methods: bot token, OAuth2 bearer token, and Basic (client_id:client_secret) only for OAuth2 token endpoints.
access_notes: Anyone can register a developer application and get client ID/secret and a bot token. Privileged intents can be toggled self-serve below 10,000 users; review is required above that. Some OAuth2 scopes are partner-only. The pages do not explicitly say 'free', so confidence is medium.
blocker_notes: Minor friction: privileged intents need review at 10,000+ users, and some scopes are approved-partner only. Neither blocks a toolkit.

evidence.quote: We support the authorization code grant, the implicit grant, client credentials, and some modified special-for-Discord flows for Bots and Webhooks.
Using a bot token found on the Bot page within your app’s settings.
Only applicable for [OAuth2 API](/developers/topics/oauth2) token endpoints.
The first step in implementing OAuth2 is [registering a developer application](https://discord.com/developers/applications) and retrieving your client ID and client secret.
If your app has fewer than 10,000 users, you may access Privileged Intents by enabling them in the Developer Portal.
To inquire about access about scopes that are only available to approved partners, speak to your Discord account representative to see if they are a fit for your needs.
